From https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Lu7nrdAU88 titled “EPIC!!🤓 HOW TO: Make a MAGETIC HOLOGRAPHIC VIEWING SUPERCELL! 💎😎” and published August 24, 2019.

Materials:

  1. Two “optical flats”, can get from eBay. Could use camera filters, ~70-75 mm, so search both.
  2. Mouse milk.
  3. Ferrofluid.
  4. Two pipettes (might order bulk if less expensive).
  5. LED ring, with black tape around it, or 3D print a casing.
  6. Clear tape.
  7. Canned air, or a “bulb pump” or perhaps even a turkey baster would work.
  8. Towel (42).
  9. Rubbing alcohol (although isopropyl 99% might be preferable).

Construction:

  1. Lay down a towel, as stuff will leak out.
  2. Wash the optical flats with soap and water, dry them, then put them next to each other on the towel, and apply alcohol to the top surface and wipe clean or just let it dry (probably better).
  3. Prepare the pipettes: in one, suck up a little mouse milk; in the other, suck up a little ferrofluid.
  4. Cut three pieces of tape about 2” long and fold about 1/2” of one end (so it can be removed easily later; this will also depend on the size of the flats you purchased).
  5. Using canned air or equivalent, get all the dust off of them.
  6. Choose one to be the lower, and put 3-4 drops of mouse milk in the center. Stir it around with the pipette a little, so it covers an area that’s around a quarter to a third of the distance from the center to the outside edge.
  7. Put one to one-and-a-half drops of ferrofluid in the center.
  8. Note that around 90% of this will squish out the sides, so the towel is important.
  9. Lift the other, and while turning it over (i.e., so that the clean top surface will be facing the fluids), hold it above and “roll” it closed. Don’t drop it straight down; make two edges meet on one side of the circle, and then slowly flatten the top flat onto the bottom one, spinning it as the fluid moves around. This is somewhat like preparing a microscope slide.
  10. The fluids may be uneven, so move the top flat in a circular motion while keeping the bottom flat motionless.
  11. There may be bubbles, so push down on the flat a millimeter or so behind the bubble, and move your fingers forward as it moves towards the edge and out. Keep doing this until all the bubbles are gone.
  12. Tape the edges in three places, like an equilateral triangle.
  13. Drop it in the LED ring case (whether 3D-printed, or made from black tape), and we’re done!

Note that these “burn out” after a little while and you'll need to take it apart, clean the glass, and can then make another one. So the initial materials can make many of these viewing devices.
